text.p: A U.S. federal judge on Thursday sentenced a livestock slaughter plant contractor to 30 months in prison for discharging fecally contaminated water into a river, the Justice Department said.

Terry Rettig, 45, operated two water treatment plants for Smithfield Foods Inc, each of which discharged a million gallons a day of waste water from hog slaughter into the Pagan River in Virginia Beach, Va.
Rettig's own business, A-T.R. Systems Management Inc, also operated smaller plants on a contract basis.
Rettig pleaded guilty in October to 23 counts of violating the Clean Water Act.

The waste water exceeded limits set in the act for fecal coliform, a bacteria found in manure and slaughterhouse waste. The bacteria is associated with pathogens known to cause serious illness in humans.
